title: Line actions offered match the line's status
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with WO Lines: Create & Edit + Full View.
2. A work order has lines in each status: Needs Approval, Approved, Declined, Complete.
steps:
1. Open the ... menu (and check the bulk bar) for a Needs Approval line.
2. Repeat for Approved, Declined and Complete lines.
expected:
1. Needs Approval: Approve, Decline, Request part, Delete line.
2. Approved: Decline, Authorization required, Complete, Request part, Delete line.
3. Declined: Approve, Authorization required, Request part, Delete line.
4. Complete: Decline, Authorization required, Uncomplete.
5. Any action not listed for a status is not visible, on the line or in the bulk action bar.
6. Complete is not offered on a Needs Approval line and Approve is not offered on an already-Approved line (both do nothing).

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9252 (Story 6, Which actions appear on a line and on a part) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 21, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Part actions offered match the part's state (seven states)
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with WO Lines: Create & Edit + Full View, Pick Parts and Order Parts.
2. Parts exist in each state: Requested, Quoted, Auth to order, In Stock (unpicked), Awaiting, Received later, Received/picked, Returned.
steps: 1. For a part in each state, look at the actions on its row.
expected:
1. Requested: nothing on the row (no price yet), but still counted in the bulk bar's Order (n).
2. Quoted: Order. Auth to order: Order.
3. In Stock and not picked: Pick.
4. Awaiting: Receive, with Received later behind its caret when receiving is required.
5. Received later: nothing on the row, Receive in the ... menu.
6. Received or picked: nothing (finished). Returned: nothing (sent back, stays visible on the line and in returns).

---

title: Ordering precedes receiving; Receive placement follows the setting
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with Order Parts.
2. A vendor-sourced part is unordered; and the receiving setting can be toggled.
steps:
1. With ordering required, check whether Receive appears before the part is ordered.
2. With receiving not required, check where Receive appears for a part.
expected:
1. With ordering required, Receive does not appear until the part has been ordered; Order and Receive are never offered at once for the same part.
2. With receiving not required, Receive moves from the part row into the part's ... menu - it is never removed outright.
3. Ordering a Requested part only does something when the part is vendor-sourced (including a vendorless part marked Vendor missing); an inventory/found part or one with no source needs its details completed first.

---

title: Declining or sending back a line returns only not-yet-arrived parts to Quoted
preconditions:

title: Bulk bar replaces the column headers and lists actions by one rule
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with WO Lines: Create & Edit + Full View.
2. A work order has several lines in mixed statuses with parts.
steps:
1. Select one or more lines.
2. Look at the bar that appears, its layout and which actions show.
expected:
1. The bar sits at the top of the list and replaces the column headers while a selection is active; nothing on the page shifts when it appears.
2. Selecting a row highlights the whole line, including its story, labour and parts.
3. Layout is: n selected, then up to three primary buttons, then More, then a close control.
4. Each action follows one rule: nothing in the selection qualifies -> hidden; something qualifies but is blocked -> shown disabled with the reason; qualifies and not blocked -> shown with its count.
5. Line actions count lines and parts actions count parts ("Receive 5 parts" may come from two lines); a count never includes what the action would skip.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9253 (Story 7, The bulk action bar) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 21, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Bulk approve/decline judges each line and never sweeps a declined line
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with WO Lines: Create & Edit + Full View.
2. A selection mixes Needs Approval, Approved, Declined and Completed lines, one holding received parts.
steps:
1. Select the mixed set and run Approve.
2. Run Decline on a selection.
3. Run Authorization required on a selection.
expected:
1. Each selected line is judged on its own by the single-line rule; every qualifying line goes through and one failure does not stop the rest.
2. A declined line is never swept up: it is left alone by Approve and by Authorization required and is not in either count.
3. Approve counts lines in Needs Approval; Decline counts lines in Needs Approval and Approved; Authorization required counts lines in Approved; completed lines are excluded from all three.
4. Approving a declined line stays possible from the line itself (only the bulk path leaves declined lines out).
5. The result names each failure with its line number and reason in one message, for example "3 lines approved. 1 line couldn't be declined: Line 3, parts must be returned first".
6. Undo restores only the lines that changed, to the status they held.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9254 (Story 8, Bulk approve and decline) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 21, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Bulk order raises a purchase order per vendor and confirms first
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with Order Parts (+ See Financial Data).
2. A selection holds unordered parts spanning two vendors, plus a Requested part and a vendorless part.
steps:
1. Select the parts and run Order.
2. Confirm and check the purchase orders created.
expected:
1. Bulk Order runs the existing single-part order once per selected part; the vendor/PO decision is the existing path.
2. A selection spanning two vendors produces a purchase order per vendor; a vendor with an open PO on this work order has its parts added to it.
3. Requested parts are included and counted alongside Quoted and Auth to order (the ordering path moves a Requested part straight to Awaiting).
4. A part with no vendor is ordered and counted like any other: the PO is created marked Vendor missing and does not sync to QuickBooks until a vendor is assigned.
5. Ordering asks for confirmation first because a purchase order is a commitment to a supplier and cannot be undone.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9257 (Story 11, Bulk order parts) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 21, read on 21 August 2026.
